active_budget.direct_one_sided_condition: Equivalently, any pointwise one-sided bounds max(0,-E_d(N))<=B_d(N) are enough when sum_d max(0,B_d(N)) < local_main(N).

candidate.falsifier: If the adverse WBSS coefficient family has substantial weight across enough nonprincipal character channels that each needs an individual pointwise binary-prime asymptotic, then this route collapses back to the known Goldbach-strength input.
candidate.mechanism: Decompose the four q286-WBSS coefficient projections into Dirichlet-character or finite Fourier modes and try to bound only the adverse signed combination, not every residue-pair channel separately.
candidate.name: signed-character budget instead of full AP uniformity
candidate.prediction: If the coefficient support is spectrally sparse or has cancellations invisible to per-residue L1, a direct one-sided character estimate may require less than full pointwise AP Goldbach.
candidate.smallest_test: Build a character-mode burden audit for the four WBSS projected coefficient families and measure whether the adverse budget is concentrated in few modes or spread across many hard channels.

decision: Known checked theorem shapes do not currently pay the q286-WBSS coefficient-discrepancy budget.  One-dimensional AP prime-count bounds miss binary correlation, average and almost-all Goldbach-in-AP results miss the every-large-N quantifier, and upper-bound/distribution results miss the required positive one-sided lower control.  The next non-finite route is a signed-character burden audit to see whether the WBSS adverse combination is narrower than full fixed-modulus pointwise Goldbach in progressions.

evaluated_sources.source: Bennett, Martin, O'Bryant, Rechnitzer, Explicit bounds for primes in arithmetic progressions
evaluated_sources.what_it_supplies: Explicit estimates for pi(x;q,a), theta(x;q,a), and psi(x;q,a) in individual prime residue classes.
evaluated_sources.why_not_enough: The q286-WBSS budget is a binary convolution/residue-pair statement for the actual partner N-p.  Marginal prime counts in p mod q do not control the signed correlation between p and N-p.

evaluated_sources.source: Bhowmik, Halupczok, Matsumoto, Suzuki, Goldbach Representations in Arithmetic Progressions and zeros of Dirichlet L-functions
evaluated_sources.what_it_supplies: Average-order Goldbach-in-progressions information and relations with zeros of Dirichlet L-functions.
evaluated_sources.why_not_enough: Average asymptotics, even when informative about zeros, do not give the every-sufficiently-large-N pointwise one-sided discrepancy bound needed here.

evaluated_sources.source: Salmensuu, The Goldbach conjecture with summands in arithmetic progressions
evaluated_sources.what_it_supplies: Almost-all representation results over moduli, residue classes, and natural numbers.
evaluated_sources.why_not_enough: Almost-all coverage does not imply the q286-WBSS pointwise bound for every sufficiently large covered even target.

evaluated_sources.source: Lichtman, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli, and Goldbach beyond the square-root barrier
evaluated_sources.what_it_supplies: Improved distribution levels for primes and applications to upper bounds for Goldbach representations.
evaluated_sources.why_not_enough: Upper bounds and level-of-distribution improvements do not provide a positive lower bound or one-sided signed discrepancy estimate for each fixed q286-WBSS target.

status_boundary: source-backed theorem adequacy audit only; it imports no proof of a q286-WBSS pointwise discrepancy theorem, threshold theorem, strict-central Goldbach theorem, or Goldbach proof

sufficient_external_theorem_shape.full_per_residue_version: For each d in {70,130,154,286}, every projected residue s, and every sufficiently large covered even N, prove |Delta_{d,s}(N)| <= eta_d(N) with sum_d L1_d*eta_d(N) < local_main(N).
sufficient_external_theorem_shape.narrow_one_sided_version: For each d, prove max(0,-E_d(N)) <= B_d(N) pointwise with sum_d max(0,B_d(N)) < local_main(N).
sufficient_external_theorem_shape.why_full_AP_asymptotic_would_be_strong: A positive pointwise asymptotic for every fixed residue-pair channel would imply the budget, but that is already a binary Goldbach-in-progressions-strength input rather than a small local q286 lemma.
